# <span id="aanchor11"></span> Sample Quality Editor

The Sample Quality Editor displays analysis samples in descending chronological order for a specified time frame. By default, the Sample Quality Editor displays the most recent month of samples.

<div class="procedure">

To enter a new sample:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Sample Analyses**.
2.  Click the **New Detail** button at the bottom of the **Sample Quality Editor** screen. This editor contains a detailed layout of a hydrocarbon analysis sample.
3.  You can enter Mole %, Mass % or LV % and have FLOWCAL calculate the other properties for the sample such as densities in different units (top right), component Mole %, Mass % and/or LV % etc. All calculations are done according to the source characteristics.
4.  You can also set a liquids product designation for the sample which in turn is used during LQ apply operations to make sure that like products are applied between the Product in the sample and the product in the meter data or batch. FLOWCAL will not do a sample apply of two disparate products.

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following tabs are available on the Sample Analysis Editor screen:

- **Quality** - Specification of quality characteristics such as product, molar mass, relative density, etc. (Alt+Q)
- **Mole %** - Sample breakdown or composition in Mole %. (Alt+M)
- **Mass %** - Sample breakdown or composition in Mass %. (Alt+A)
- **LV %** - Sample breakdown or composition in LV %. (Alt+L)
- **C6+** - Specification of C6+ extended characteristics such as molar mass, absolute density, relative density, etc. (Alt+C)
- **Sample** - Sample attributes such as sample pressure, temperature, atmospheric pressure, etc. (Alt+S)
- **Custom** - User-defined fields. (Alt+U)
- **Edit Reasons** - Edit reasons allows the user to see who changed a sample, when it was changed, and the reason for changing the sample. (Alt+E)

HC Properties Override allows the user to select a given set of GPA TP-17 hydrocarbon properties to be used in calculations, including user-defined sets.

</div>
